stories.analysis: Coverage of this Pentagon watchdog report spanned roughly four bias points, with left-leaning and center-left outlets emphasizing political dissent and economic harm to ordinary Americans, while right-leaning outlets foregrounded threat and fiscal burden framing. At the left end, the Guardian and Newsweek focused on GOP fracture, using phrases like "turning on Iran war" and "Republican Rebellion," casting opposition as an electoral warning sign rather than engaging the watchdog report's substance. CNBC extended this toward consumer harm, framing war costs as a "one-two punch" hitting households. Neutral outlets — BBC, The Hill, Boston Globe — anchored on the inspector general's findings directly, using plain constructions like "confirms," "details US losses," and "Pentagon tells Congress." At the right end, the Daily Caller employed notably charged language: "Massive Toll" and "Reveals" implied concealment, while a second Daily Caller headline recast the same cost figure as "Costing Taxpayers" who "Struggle to Afford Basic Needs," shifting emphasis from governmental accountability to citizen victimhood.
